newsitem.title: ITALY: IRI sees capital gains from Stet.
newsitem.headline: IRI sees capital gains from Stet.

text.p: Italian industrial holding IRI said on Monday the transfer of its stake in telephone concern Stet to the Treasury would generate a capital gain of around 3.496 trillion lire ($2.3 billion) in 1996.

The Treasury earlier said it would pay IRI at least 14.53 trillion lire to take over its controlling stake in Stet. IRI holds 61.27 percent of Stet's ordinary shares. The exact sum to be paid by the Treasury to IRI has not yet been fixed.
IRI, which is forecast to make a loss of up to three trillion lire in 1996, gave the capital gains projection in a statement issued after a board meeting.
Under the Stet share transfer, the Treasury will pay IRI three trillion lire by the end of December and the rest by the end of June 1997. But it stressed IRI can only use the money to reduce debts.

IRI has current debt of some 23.5 trillion lire. Under a 1993 accord with the European Union, IRI must cut its debt to below five trillion lire by the end of the year from its end-1995 level of 22.5 trillion.
